newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: EU states ask for more "accurate" telecoms grades.
newsitem.headline: EU states ask for more "accurate" telecoms grades.

text.p: European Union telecommunications ministers asked the European Commission on Friday to prepare an "updated and more accurate" report on their efforts to open telecoms markets to competition.
Some EU countries were disappointed at a recent Commission report grouping countries according to how well they had complied with the EU's plan to abolish telecoms monopolies by January 1, 1998.
The study, issued in May, gave Britain, Denmark, Finland and Sweden top marks, while saying progress was slowest in Belgium, Greece, Portugal and Spain.
Some of the low-ranking countries argued that it did not give them credit for recent initiatives, diplomats and officials said.

"The report was already outdated by the time it was published," Dutch Public Works Minister Annemarie Jorritsma-Lebbink, who chaired the meeting, told reporters. She said the data had been compiled several months earlier.
She said the ministers agreed to work with the Commission to ensure it had up-to-date information when it publishes its next report.
Portugal was among the angriest countries, complaining that its liberalisation efforts had been damaged by reports in the media that it was among the worst offenders, one official said.
But Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert said the Commission had actually taken a diplomatic approach, overlooking some violations of EU law, he added.
Commission spokesman Jochen Kubosch told reporters the EU executive would publish a new report in time for the next meeting of EU telecoms ministers in October.
